name: slide-sections
body: Section nesting comes from heading depth: a `# name` heading starts a section of the slide, a `## name` heading opens a child section of the most recent `#` section, a `###` a child of the most recent `##`, and so on down to `######`. A section runs until the next heading at the same or a shallower depth, or end of file. Content between the slide's `---` frontmatter and the first heading is the slide's own body, not a section. `# notes` stays top-level only (a deeper heading never starts notes). Inside a section whose template declares child sections, a heading one level deeper must name one of those declared child sections; any other name is an error suggesting the closest match. Inside a section whose template declares no child sections, deeper headings stay ordinary Markdown subheadings, governed by the template's `body.subheadings` rule. A section name must be declared by its parent's template (the slide template for a top-level section, the parent section's template for a child); an undeclared name = error with a closest-match suggestion; a repeat count outside the declared min/max = error, counted per parent instance (nested-section-validation).
